messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert: KV cache growth + NCCL stalls on tp-shard pool (region-us-west-2). Memory climb + >50% requests hitting 5-20s tails. Auto-escalation: paging oncall. https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/kv_cache

incident-bot: Affected services: text-generation (hosted), some Dedicated customers in us-west-2. Potential root: uneven tensor-parallel KV partitioning + continuous-batching amplification.

sara (oncall): I'm paged, looking now. grabbing logs from the shard hosts. @michael if you can stand by for handoff in 10m in case I need deeper kernel work.

michael: standing by. any initial impact on customers?

sara (oncall): Liz says two customers reported massive latency spikes and request timeouts ~40m ago. CS notes: no data loss, but visible 5x latency and some 429s due to per-node memory pressure.

liz (cs): confirmed. Customer A (enterprise-dash) saw >=50 failed requests during the window, Customer B (playground customer) saw sporadic 503s. Both on tp-shard pool in us-west-2.

jia: grabbing dmesg + gpu logs from node tp-gpu-07. Seeing repeated NCCL_TIMEOUTs and one GPU OOM. Logs:```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] NCCL WARN NET/IB : NCCL WARN: Timeout waiting for unexpected message
[2026-03-15T14:12:04Z] GPU0: OutOfMemory allocating 512MB (kv_cache shard 3)
[2026-03-15T14:12:04Z] nvml: process killed due to signal 9
```

alex: interesting — the KV cache metrics show one shard holding ~3x keys vs others for some prefixes. Looks like partitioning hash skew or incorrect TP shard index calc.

eng-runtime: we just rolled a minor change earlier to continuous batching heuristics that increases max prefix window from 64->256 for longer in-flight contexts. Could amplify memory by holding more KV entries concurrently.

sara (oncall): plan: 1) disable continuous batching on tp-shard pool (hotfix config) 2) reduce max_batch_size temporarily 3) restart the affected agents gracefully 4) investigate shard assignment calc & NCCL config.

michael: agree. quick callout: disabling continuous batching is low-risk and should free KV retention. Who can flip config?

infra-kv-team: we can flip a runtime flag via env override. Endpoint: /api/v1/runtime/flags. Will do a canary on tp-gpu-01 then roll.

infra-kv-team: PATCH /api/v1/runtime/flags {"continuous_batching": false} -> applied to tp-gpu-01. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Deploy event: runtime-flag-update by infra-kv-team. Canary started on tp-gpu-01.

jia: after canary disabled, observed KV cache resident size drop ~28% on tp-gpu-01 within 2m. NCCL errors reduced on that host.

alex: rolling to rest of tp-shard pool now. also lowering `max_batch_size` from 64->32 for the pool.

sara (oncall): commands used for roll (internal):```bash
# disable continuous batching for pool tp-shard
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/runtime/flags \
  -d '{"pools": ["tp-shard"], "continuous_batching": false, "max_batch_size": 32}'
```

michael: keep the restarts graceful. prefer draining non-blocking and letting clients failover. Also set NCCL_TIMEOUT longer as temporary mitigation.

infra-kv-team: increased NCCL_TIMEOUT to 300000 (ms) on cluster via sysctl override. Rolling restart scheduled with 30s drain.

eng-runtime: after flags rolled, tail latency improved to near baseline, but one node still shows memory pressure. Hypothesis: uneven partitioning left a hot shard that won't drop unless restarted.

sara (oncall): ok, isolate node tp-gpu-07 and restart its agent. Doing a graceful restart now.

incident-bot: Action logged: drain tp-gpu-07 -> restart agent -> rejoin.

jia: restart complete. Post-restart KV distribution rebalanced, shard sizes across GPUs normalized. NCCL stalls cleared.

liz (cs): Customer A reporting recovery, error rate dropped to normal. Thanks. :tada:

michael: good. immediate mitigation worked: continuous batching off + lower batch size + restart + NCCL timeout bump. Need root cause: why partitioning skewed?

eng-runtime: preliminary diff shows a math bug in the TP shard index calculation introduced in recent tensor-parallel refactor: integer divide vs floor mismatch when using 64-bit counters. In some prefix hashes, shard index computed as (hash % (tp_world_size-1)) rather than % tp_world_size, causing some shards to be skipped and others overloaded.

alex: that would explain uneven partitioning. Combined with continuous batching holding long prefix windows, the hot shard amassed lots of KV entries and then OOMed, causing NCCL instability.

infra-kv-team: opened PR #4923 to fix index calc and added unit tests for modulo with various world sizes. Also added a canary to assert kv shard counts per node remain within 20% of mean during rollout.

michael: add an exp catch in runtime to refuse to start with kv imbalance > 3x until operator approves.

eng-runtime: added a guard: if shard_count_max > shard_count_mean * 3 then log error and disable continuous batching. Will include in follow-up patch.

sara (oncall): summary for postmortem:
- Impact: P1 latency spikes and request failures for two customers; no data loss.
- Root cause: tensor-parallel KV shard index calc bug + continuous batching config change increased KV retention. Combined -> hot-shard OOM -> NCCL stalls.
- Mitigations applied: disabled continuous batching (hotfix), reduced max_batch_size, increased NCCL_TIMEOUT, restarted hot node, rolled fixed flag cluster-wide.
- Long term fixes: patch index calc in PR #4923, add rollout canary for shard balance, add runtime guard to prevent excessive imbalance, add load tests with skewed prefix distributions.

liz (cs): customers notified; CS follow-ups scheduled.

michael: will own follow-up postmortem. action items assigned in tracker: IN-1024 (postmortem), IN-1025 (fix & tests), IN-1026 (canary checks), IN-1027 (load test).

sara (oncall): handing off to @michael in 10m for next-day oncall and follow-ups. Thanks team. :heart:

incident-bot: Incident closed (status: mitigated). Logged timeline and actions to incident system.
